podcast.title: Founding and Early Style (1926)
podcast.body: The Soul Stirrers originated in 1926, performing in the "Jubilee Style," a manner of singing spiritual music common among black singers before Thomas Dorsey's revolution in gospel. "The Soul Sturlers had started out in 1926 as a group in what was called The Jubilee Style."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: Live Performance Popularity (1955)
podcast.body: The Soul Stirrers were notably more popular as a live act than as a recording act, a characteristic evident in a 1955 live recording produced by Bumps Blackwell. "The soul-sturvers were more popular as a live-act than as a recording act, and hearing the live recording of them that Bumps Blackwell produced in 1955, it's easy to see why."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: Financial Performance as a Gospel Group
podcast.body: In 1956, the group's record sales were in the "low tens of thousands," which was considered a reasonable amount for a gospel group but insufficient to generate significant wealth for its members. "The soul-sturvers were only selling in the low tens of thousands. A reasonable amount for a gospel group but hardly the kinds of numbers that would make anyone rich."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: Popular Spiritual Group
podcast.body: The Soul Stirrers were a very popular spiritual group, fronted by Sam Cooke, during the time Aretha Franklin toured the country with her father in the mid-1950s. Franklin befriended them during this period. "Around this time, while touring the country with her father, Aretha Franklin befriended the very popular spiritual group The Soul Sturs, fronted by the fast-rising gospel heartthrob Sam Cook."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Say a Little Prayer Edition Part 1

podcast.title: Transition to New Gospel Style
podcast.body: Following Thomas Dorsey's innovation in gospel music, The Soul Stirrers successfully adapted their style, becoming one of the first and most acclaimed gospel quartets in this new format. "The Soul Sturlers switched styles and became one of the first and best gospel quartets in the new style."
